# Self-service Postcards — 23 October 2026

## Owner scope

During the story-editor extension, the owner requested automatic subscriber mail on publication OR an editable admin email template with Send/Schedule. The selected implementation is the latter: Prepare a Postcard from a currently published entry, edit the private draft, save/preview, explicitly confirm its exact content/audience, and then request Send/Schedule. Publishing alone sends no email. This preserves the deliberate Wednesday cadence while allowing an owner-requested extra campaign. The owner then said to continue. Production publication/activation is still pending review; no immediate, test or subscriber send is authorized for this build.

## Implemented boundary

- Postcards tab contains a branded editable template, subject/preheader, headline/body, public canonical CTA, optional already-public website image, private cross-device draft saving, HTML download, an inert preview isolated in a shadow root, and job status. Prepare a Postcard uses the saved public projection, not unsaved/private story edits. There is no automatic AI-generated personal content.
- Save/preview do not create campaigns or send mail. Staging subscriber delivery is forbidden in both UI and database Rules. Production requires the reviewed CMS namespace release, an explicit repository activation flag, main-branch worker and an IAM-only enabled delivery configuration. Buttons explain unavailability instead of simulating success.
- Future explicit delivery creates one immutable job per Postcard draft; its reviewed payload/revision must match the saved draft. Jobs cannot be recreated or edited to resend. A still-queued request can be cancelled with a transaction before worker claim. After processing starts, the UI directs the owner to Brevo for provider-level review/changes. Editing a saved draft does not change a queued/scheduled campaign.
- A new scheduled GitHub Actions job reuses the existing Firebase service-account and Brevo secrets. Repository visibility was read back as public; standard hosted runners are used. It does not require Codex, an open browser, a local computer, Cloud Run, a Storage bucket, a new credential, paid billing or contact imports. A main/public-repository/explicit activation gate prevents delivery in this review release.
- The worker reads only bounded queued/processing job snapshots, validates all strings/URLs/enums, verifies the linked production publication/page, existing free plan/sender, and the saved active-subscriber segment #1 with a pinned provider modification timestamp. If that segment changes, delivery stops for owner review. The API exposes segment metadata, not full criteria; the earlier owner-approved Subscribed AND existing list #3 conditions remain a provider configuration to preserve. Brevo campaign suppression remains active; no transactional bulk-mail workaround, subscriber export or resubscription is used.
- Provider campaign names include the immutable request ID. CAS claims, phase markers and bounded reconciliation precede mutations. An ambiguous create/dispatch is held for review and is not automatically repeated. Only matching new managed campaign IDs can be modified. Existing campaigns #8/#9/#11 are not edited. Provider acceptance/scheduling is distinguished from inbox delivery.
- Dates are explicitly Europe/Amsterdam, not the device timezone. Missing/ambiguous daylight-saving times are rejected. Admin schedules require 1 hour to 90 days ahead; worker holds a missed/too-close time instead of sending late. Background processing can be delayed. Once accepted, the actual schedule lives in Brevo. Immediate Send is a queued background request, not an instant-delivery guarantee.
- The template is shared by browser and worker, escapes all owner strings, uses a fixed public CTA policy, keeps unsubscribe/privacy/support and free branding. No browser credential, private photo/data URL, raw HTML injection, paid API or additional tracking is introduced. Optional email images currently require an existing canonical /assets/ URL; Firestore-hosted new photos are not silently uploaded to Brevo.

## Checks and activation

No automated tests or campaign send were run. Syntax, Rules compilation and the read-only workflow check are used. The actual mail lifecycle and inbox delivery remain unexercised. A check can read existing provider metadata and write only disabled staging availability; it cannot create/schedule/send a campaign. Production activation requires a separate reviewed release, POSTCARDS_DELIVERY_ENABLED=true in the repository and an explicit main workflow activate action. Keep old Codex senders paused and calendar reminder mail disabled. Do not activate simply because a draft preview looks correct.

## Release evidence and connection history

- The Postcard editor deployed in successful staging Hosting runs 40010250549 (3c9204a), 40010640375 (4f6df61) and 40011113949 (4830797). A readback found the deployed mail module/model/template identical to source after line-ending normalization. Staging admin remains noindex; the report URL returns 404; production admin contains neither new editor.
- The shared branded template was visually observed locally using already-public Philippines content. The example is explicitly labelled as a local preview with nothing saved or sent. Its screenshot is outside source. An actual authenticated private-draft cycle and marketing-campaign lifecycle have not been exercised.
- Read-only provider checks stop safely before any campaign mutation. Runs 40010640485 and 40011113520 reported HTTP 403 at GET /v3/account. The bounded diagnostic refinement at 9e51971, run 40012197538, confirmed provider code permission_denied without exposing response bodies, account records, content or credentials.
- Initially, read-only Brevo UI observation found exactly one existing active, restricted API key named Website question notifications, with Transactional email: All only. This explained the denied account request. Additional Email campaigns: All (the UI has no smaller create/send permission), Contacts: Read and Account: Read were prepared but not saved until explicit owner approval. See the completed follow-up below, which supersedes this initial blocker.
- Initially, API IP blocking was active. After scope approval, run 40012197538 attempt 2 confirmed an HTTP401 refusal due to the server IP. The owner then explicitly approved disabling API IP blocking after being told that this affects all API keys and allows a valid key from any IP. Do not describe this security tradeoff as a new isolation boundary or a static server address.

## Owner-approved connection completed

- The owner explicitly approved the three added API permissions. Brevo requested its own emailed verification code; the owner entered it privately and confirmed completion. A fresh edit-form read showed the exact four saved scopes, unchanged expiry and disabled Save changes. No new credential was created or copied. The key value was never exposed.
- The owner separately approved disabling the API IP block, with its account-wide impact explained. The Brevo confirmation was completed; fresh UI readback shows API keys: Deactivated. SMTP state was already Deactivated and was not changed. Authorized address lists were not edited. GitHub standard runner addresses vary; their broad IP ranges were not added as an allowlist. Existing question alerts also use this account API boundary; do not silently re-enable it and break unattended jobs.
- After the approved IP change, the account request passed but the sender request received a non-JSON403 (attempt 3 of run 40012197538). Commit 2ca1b28 identifies the real Postcards client with User-Agent and requests JSON; safe fixed-category diagnostics remain bounded and never log response bodies. The next bounded read-only run **40020203215 succeeded**: existing free plan, active verified sender and saved subscriber segment were found; the bounded outbox query completed and disabled staging delivery settings were written. This confirms configuration access, not a created campaign or inbox delivery.
- The production activation repository flag was read back as absent/off before the checks. No production mail configuration was enabled. Staging send/schedule remain denied. No campaign was created, edited, scheduled or dispatched during this work; the only new email interaction was Brevo's native owner-security verification. Existing subscriber campaigns and calendar reminder preferences were not changed. A previously scheduled campaign #11 showed Sent in Brevo's activity feed at 23 October 11:05; that was an existing independent schedule, not a send from this build. Do not duplicate it or infer individual inbox receipt.
- The provider connection blocker is resolved. The subsequently completed authenticated CMS and private Postcard checks are recorded below. The marketing-delivery lifecycle remains unexercised. Production release/activation still requires separate owner approval; no passwords, OTPs or browser tokens were inspected.

## Authenticated template check completed

- Prepare a Postcard copied the currently published title/excerpt/link while an unsaved private story title was different. Save, reload and reopen retained the private template fields. Editing invalidated the preview and consent.
- The initial iframe preview was blank in the real signed-in admin. Both srcdoc and a temporary Blob approach were observed blank; no specific browser-header cause was established. Commit 7ccf3f8 replaces it with direct inert rendering of the same escaped shared template through a strict DOM allowlist in a shadow root. Scripts, frames, forms, event attributes, active links and noncanonical images are excluded; existing framing/security headers were not weakened. Preview links are deliberately inactive and explained in the UI.
- The final actual admin preview visibly rendered brand, headline, body and the selected public photograph; the image was decoded. DOM observation found no active link href, script, iframe or form inside the preview. Editing cleared/hid it; private save succeeded. The staging Send/Schedule buttons stayed disabled even when consent was checked, and consent was reset afterward.
- One clearly named private staging Postcard verification draft remains; no mail job or campaign was created, scheduled or sent. There was no subscriber or test email. Provider configuration access is verified separately, not marketing delivery/inbox receipt.
- Details and actual screenshots are recorded outside Hosting source in self-service-signed-in-check-2026-10-24.md. Final functional staging Hosting run 40025483858 succeeded at d01c64b. Production remains unchanged and delivery activation remains off.
